scenes.narration: Here's something I keep seeing. You ask a coding agent for an app, and it happily writes a login system, a content model and a search engine. From scratch. Again.

scenes.callout: Code is cheap. Owning it isn't.
scenes.narration: Generating code got cheap. Owning it didn't. Every line your agent writes is a line someone has to secure, debug and maintain.
Meanwhile, open-source platforms have spent decades on exactly these problems. Millions of sites, a huge security community, and a patching process that already works.
And here's the thing: agents are great at wiring proven pieces together. That's where they shine. Rebuilding those pieces is where the cost and the risk come from.
So start every project with one question: what can we reuse? Users, permissions, content, search. Then let the agent spend its effort on what makes your app unique.

points: Code is cheap, owning it isn't
scenes.narration: Code is cheap, owning it isn't. Reuse what's proven. And build what's actually unique.
That's what we're exploring at Proven Lab. Tell me in the comments what your agents keep rebuilding. See you in the next one.
